Cell: Introduction of cell, concepts of prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The cell is the basic structural and functional unit of life. Cell theory (Schleiden, Schwann, Virchow) unifies all organisms. Cells are grouped into prokaryotes (no true nucleus; bacteria, cyanobacteria) and eukaryotes (true nucleus and membrane-bound organelles; plants, animals). Mastering their structural differences — nucleus, ribosome type, cell wall, organelles — is a core NEB examination point.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: A virus is not a cell and is not prokaryotic or eukaryotic; it is an acellular, obligate intracellular parasite.  ·  Prokaryotes lack a nuclear membrane but still carry DNA (usually a single circular chromosome).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: NEB often asks a two-column prokaryote/eukaryote table; always include ribosome size (70S vs 80S).  ·  Mention Mycoplasma (smallest cell) and the ostrich egg (largest) to add marks.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: E. coli is a classic prokaryotic model organism.  ·  The onion root-tip cell is the standard school example of a plant eukaryotic cell.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Mycoplasma has no cell wall; it is the smallest known living cell (0.1-0.3 µm), not the smallest living organism overall.  ·  A eukaryotic nucleus is a true membrane-bound organelle; the nucleoid of a bacterium is not.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Tabulate prokaryote vs eukaryote (6 points)  ·  Label a bacterium

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: PRO = small, NO nucleus; EU = nucleus + organelles.  ·  Ribosome 7-0 (seventy) = prokaryote; 8-0 = eukaryote.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Why are prokaryotes called "lower" organisms?  ·  State two features present only in eukaryotes.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Prokaryote/eukaryote comparison table is a very common short-answer.  ·  State cell theory fully (3 postulates + names).

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Cell theory  ·  Prokaryote vs eukaryote  ·  Cell wall types  ·  Selective permeability

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Cell = smallest structural + functional unit of life.  ·  Prokaryote: no nucleus, 70S ribosomes, circular DNA, cell wall usually peptidoglycan.  ·  Eukaryote: membrane-bound nucleus, 80S ribosomes, linear chromosomes, organelles.  ·  Three postulates of cell theory (Schleiden, Schwann, Virchow).

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: The largest cell is the ostrich egg; the smallest living cell is Mycoplasma.  ·  Human ova (~0.12 mm) are visible to the naked eye; the sperm head is ~5 µm long.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: If a specimen has a cell wall, chloroplasts and a nucleus, is it plant, animal or fungal? Justify.  ·  Explain the significance of the plasma membrane being selectively permeable.  ·  Compare the 70S and 80S ribosomes.

rows.label: More hints
rows.text: Describe the structure of a typical bacterium with a labelled diagram.  ·  Explain why viruses are not considered living cells.

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: Amoeba is a single eukaryotic cell that carries out all life functions.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: Which feature is present only in eukaryotic cells? → C  ·  The smallest known living cell is: → A

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: Cell theory (Schleiden, Schwann, Virchow): all organisms are made of one or more cells; the cell is the basic structural and functional unit; every cell arises from a pre-existing cell.  ·  Cell = the smallest unit of life; bounded by the plasma membrane; size typically 1-100 µm.  ·  Prokaryotic cell: no membrane-bound nucleus or organelles; 70S ribosomes; e.g. bacteria, cyanobacteria; smaller (1-10 µm).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Ribosome types  ·  Smallest/largest cell  ·  Cell wall: plants (cellulose), fungi (chitin), bacteria (peptidoglycan); absent in animals.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Viruses are acellular; they are NOT classified as cells.  ·  Cell walls are found in plants, fungi and most bacteria; they are ABSENT in animal cells.  ·  Stress that a "cell" must carry out metabolism to be considered the unit of life.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Memorise cell-theory postulates and the three scientists.  ·  Learn the ribosome size distinction (70S prokaryotes, 80S eukaryotes).  ·  Draw and label a bacterium and an animal/plant cell.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Keep a two-column prokaryote vs eukaryote table for quick revision.  ·  All known living organisms are cellular.  ·  A prokaryote is the simplest true cell; a eukaryote is the most complex.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: The plasma membrane is selectively permeable and controls the entry of materials.  ·  Cell theory has three postulates and is the foundation of modern biology.  ·  Cell wall: Plant (cellulose), Fungi (chitin), Bacteria (peptidoglycan), Animal (none).
